lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are setting up an isolated Google Cloud environment for a new data science team. The team must experiment with machine learning models in short-lived projects and needs full administrative access. All team members are in the same group.  
  
Your solution must limit resource creation to the `us-east1` region and permit only BigQuery and Cloud Storage. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations and allowed services, and apply it to the folder. Grant the Owner IAM role to the group at the folder level.

Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations and allowed services, and apply it to the folder. Grant the BigQuery Admin and Storage Admin IAM roles to the group at the folder level.
Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations, and apply it to the folder. Grant the Owner IAM role to the group at the folder level.

Create a new folder. Create an organization policy with constraints to restrict resource locations, and apply it to the folder. Grant the BigQuery Admin and Storage Admin IAM roles to the group at the folder level.

questions.explanation: A folder provides a common hierarchy node for the team’s short-lived projects, so organization policies applied there govern descendant projects. The resource-locations constraint can allow only `us-east1`, and the Restrict Resource Service Usage constraint can allowlist BigQuery and Cloud Storage. The Owner role provides broad project and resource administration, whereas BigQuery Admin and Storage Admin do not provide full administrative access across the project.

questions.domain: Deploying and implementing a cloud solution
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Cloud Billing administrator for your organization. Your organization uses many Google Cloud projects and must implement a cost-control mechanism. Project teams need to be notified promptly as their spending nears its limit. You need to deliver near-real-time notifications to a team’s Slack channel when its project’s spending reaches a predefined budget threshold. The solution must be simple to support and require minimal maintenance. What should you do?

options.text: Create a detailed billing export to BigQuery. Create a Cloud Composer directed acyclic graph (DAG) that runs on a schedule to analyze the BigQuery data and post notifications to Slack.
Create a programmatic budget notification to send messages to a Pub/Sub topic. Create a Cloud Run function that is triggered by messages on the topic and posts the notifications to Slack.
Create a programmatic budget notification to send messages to a Pub/Sub topic. Create a Compute Engine managed instance group to pull messages from the Pub/Sub subscription and post them to Slack.
Create a detailed billing export to BigQuery. Create a Cloud Scheduler job that triggers a Cloud Run function to analyze the BigQuery data and post notifications to Slack.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Billing budgets can send programmatic notifications to a Pub/Sub topic, and a Pub/Sub-triggered Cloud Run function can process those events and forward them to Slack. This is a fully managed, event-driven design that avoids the scheduled latency of BigQuery analysis and the operational overhead of managing Compute Engine instances.

**Learn more:** [Set up programmatic notifications | Cloud Billing](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets-programmatic-notifications) · [Listen to your Pub/Sub notifications | Cloud Billing](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/listen-to-notifications)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team manages several petabytes of historical, structured transaction data in Apache Avro format on-premises. You are migrating this data to Google Cloud for a machine learning project. You must ensure the data can be accessed for large-scale analysis and model training with BigQuery. You must also minimize storage costs and avoid the overhead of loading the data into BigQuery-managed storage. What should you do?

options.text: Use the BigQuery Data Transfer Service to ingest all Avro files into a BigQuery native table.
Migrate the data to a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance, and use BigQuery federated queries to access the data.
Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and define a BigQuery external table partitioned by a relevant column.
Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, define a schema, and then use the bq load command to upload files individually.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery external tables can query Apache Avro files directly in Cloud Storage, keeping the data outside BigQuery-managed storage. Partitioning the external data enables partition pruning for relevant analyses, while Cloud Storage provides economical storage options for large historical datasets.

**Learn more:** [Create Cloud Storage external tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-data-cloud-storage) · [Introduction to external tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/external-tables)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team stores its container images in Artifact Registry. You need to create a new Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster and deploy these containers. An IAM service account with the required permissions to pull images from Artifact Registry has already been configured. You must make sure that the images can be deployed to the GKE cluster. What should you do?

options.text: In the Pod manifest, enter the service account name in the serviceAccountName field.
Enable Workload Identity Federation for GKE on the cluster.
Deploy the cluster nodes with the specified service account.
After creating the cluster, store the service account JSON key in a Kubernetes Secret.

questions.explanation:
GKE nodes authenticate when pulling private images from Artifact Registry. The node service account therefore needs the Artifact Registry Reader permission and must be configured as the service account for the cluster nodes. Pod service accounts and Workload Identity Federation address application workload access, rather than the node-level image-pull operation.

**Learn more:** [Deploying to Google Kubernetes Engine](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/integrate-gke) · [Configure GKE node service accounts](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/security/configure-node-service-accounts)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a business-critical backend application that runs on a Compute Engine managed instance group (MIG). The operations team needs a near-real-time notification when the average CPU utilization across every instance in the MIG exceeds 75% continuously for five minutes. You need to implement a scalable Google Cloud solution that fulfills this monitoring requirement. What should you do?

options.text: Create a logs-based metric in Cloud Logging that filters for high CPU usage entries, and then create a Cloud Monitoring alert policy based on that custom metric.

Deploy the Ops Agent to all Compute Engine VM instances to collect the CPU metric. Use a custom script running on a separate Compute Engine instance to poll this metric every five minutes, and send an email notification if the threshold is breached.
Create a Cloud Monitoring alerting policy that targets the compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization metric. Set the threshold to 75% and the duration to five minutes.
Configure an autoscaling policy for the MIG to use a CPU utilization target of 75% for five minutes, and then enable a notification channel in the autoscaler settings.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Monitoring provides the built-in `compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization` metric and metric-threshold alerting policies support both a threshold and a five-minute retest window. The relevant MIG instance time series can be combined with mean aggregation to evaluate average CPU utilization across the group; a value above `0.75` for five minutes opens an incident and can notify the operations team. This avoids custom log processing, polling infrastructure, and misuse of autoscaling.

**Learn more:** [Create metric-threshold alerting policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerts/using-alerting-ui) · [Behavior of metric-based alerting policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerts/concepts-indepth)

You manage a fleet of data storage solutions for your company on Google Cloud, including Bigtable, Cloud SQL, Memorystore, and Spanner. You need one unified view to monitor the health of every data storage solution and identify any that are at risk of downtime. What should you do?

options.text: Use Dataplex Universal Catalog to search the metadata of the data storage solutions to obtain the required insights.
Use the terraform state list command in the directory used to deploy the data storage solutions.
In the Google Cloud Console, use Cloud Asset Inventory to see an overview of the data storage solutions.
In the Google Cloud Console, navigate to Database Center to find an overview of the data storage solutions.

questions.explanation:
Database Center provides a centralized dashboard for database-fleet health across Bigtable, Cloud SQL, Memorystore, and Spanner. It aggregates health issues, including availability configuration, and helps identify databases that are most at risk of downtime.

**Learn more:** [Database Center overview](https://cloud.google.com/database-center/docs/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are deploying a new application on a Compute Engine VM instance. The application must store operational logs in a Cloud Storage bucket named `project-logs-us-central1` and be able to create new objects (logs) in that bucket. It must be restricted from modifying or deleting existing objects and from accessing any other buckets in the Google Cloud project. You must configure access according to the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.text: Create a dedicated service account for the application. Grant this service account the predefined roles/storage.objectCreator IAM role on the project-logs-us-central1 Cloud Storage bucket. Attach the service account to the Compute Engine VM instance.
Grant the Compute Engine default service account the predefined roles/storage.objectAdmin IAM role on the Google Cloud project.

Create a dedicated service account for the application. Generate a service account key, and grant the service account the predefined roles/storage.adm in IAM role on the project-logs-us-central1 Cloud Storage bucket. Store the key file on the Compute Engine VM.
Grant the Compute Engine default service account the predefined roles/storage.objectCreator IAM role on the Google Cloud project. Attach the service account to the Compute Engine VM instance.

questions.explanation:
The Storage Object Creator role (`roles/storage.objectCreator`) can be granted directly on a bucket and permits creating objects without permission to view, delete, or overwrite them. Assigning it only on `project-logs-us-central1` limits access to that bucket, and attaching a dedicated service account to the VM supplies short-lived workload credentials without storing a service account key.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/storage) · [Identity and Access Management for Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are establishing a standard process to manage team access to hundreds of Google Cloud resources. Your organization uses Cloud Identity as its primary identity provider, and you want to base access on team membership. You need a solution that makes granting and revoking access easier as individuals join and leave teams. The solution must minimize administrative effort and follow Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.text: For each team, create a Google Group in Cloud Identity with the cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum group property label. Add team members to the group, and use the group in IAM policies.
For each team, create a service account. Grant each team member the IAM permission to impersonate that service account.
For each team, create a service account. Grant each team member the IAM permission to generate and download keys for that service account.

For each team, create a Google Group in Cloud Identity with the cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum and cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.security group property labels. Add team members to the group, and use the group in IAM policies.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Identity security groups are intended for controlling access to organizational resources. Granting IAM roles to a group lets all members inherit those roles, so adding or removing a member updates their effective access without editing IAM policies for each individual. A Cloud Identity security group is a Google Group with both `cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.discussion_forum` and `cloudidentity.googleapis.com/groups.security` labels.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for using Google groups](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/groups-best-practices) · [Creating security groups](https://cloud.google.com/identity/docs/how-to/update-group-to-security-group)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a Google Cloud organization policy administrator for a company operating in a regulated industry. You must enforce a policy that restricts all new location-based Google Cloud resources to only the `australia-southeast1` and `australia-southeast2` regions. You want this policy to require minimal configuration. What should you do?

options.text: Create a custom organization policy that uses the resource.location == ‘australia-southeast1’ || resource.location == ‘australia-southeast2’ Common Expression Language (CEL) condition.
Modify the gcp.resourceLocations list constraint by adding in:australia-locations to the allowed_values list.
Modify the gcp.resourceLocations list constraint by adding in:australia-locations to the denied_values list.
Create a custom organization policy that uses the resource.location.startsWith(‘australia’) Common Expression Language (CEL) condition.

questions.explanation:
The `gcp.resourceLocations` managed list constraint supports Google-curated location value groups. Adding `in:australia-locations` to `allowed_values` permits the Australia location group, which contains `australia-southeast1` and `australia-southeast2`, while restricting new location-based resources to those locations. This is simpler and more maintainable than a custom CEL policy.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Organization policy constraints](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/org-policy-constraints)

questions.domain: Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building and deploying an application on Cloud Run that uses Cloud SQL for data storage. You must track how many database connections the application creates to ensure database connections are reused. What should you do?

options.text: In Cloud Monitoring, create a custom metric that tracks the creation of Cloud Run instances, and display the metric on a dashboard.
Log each new database connection in the application. In Cloud Monitoring, create a custom metric for these logs, and display the metric on a dashboard.
In the Google Cloud console, navigate to the Cloud SQL instance, and review the instance logs.
In Cloud Trace, enable trace storage for your project, and use a filter to check for new database connections.

questions.explanation:
Log each database-connection creation in the application and use a counter log-based metric to count the matching entries. Log-based metrics convert matching log records into Cloud Monitoring metrics, which can be displayed on a dashboard, directly measuring new connections created by the application.

**Learn more:** [Log-based metrics overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/logs-based-metrics) · [Display metric data on a custom dashboard](https://docs.cloud.google.com/monitoring/charts)

questions.domain: Deploying and implementing a cloud solution
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A development team has packaged and pushed a new container image to Artifact Registry. Because of design requirements, the application must be able to scale to zero. You need to move this image to production as quickly as possible while meeting those design requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Create an instance template for the container, and use it to create a managed instance group behind an external Application Load Balancer.
Create an app.yaml file that specifies the container images, and deploy it to the App Engine Flexible environment.
Write a Kubernetes Deployment and a Service manifest (YAML), and apply them to a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster.
Deploy the application directly to Cloud Run.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Run directly deploys supported container images from Artifact Registry and automatically removes even the final instance when there are no incoming requests, providing scale-to-zero behavior. This makes it the fastest managed deployment option that satisfies the requirement.

**Learn more:** [Deploy container images to Cloud Run services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/deploying) · [What is Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/overview/what-is-cloud-run)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You administer Identity and Access Management (IAM) for your Google Cloud project. A new developer has joined the cloud-developer team and needs to deploy containerized applications to an existing Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. They do not need to manage the GKE cluster itself or any other cloud resources. Following the principle of least privilege, what should you do?

options.text: Add the developer to the cloud-developer group that already has the container.developer IAM role.
Grant the developer the container.admin IAM role for the project.
Grant the developer the container.serviceAgent IAM role for the project.
Grant the developer the editor IAM role for the project.

questions.explanation:
The Kubernetes Engine Developer role (`roles/container.developer`) provides access to Kubernetes API objects within GKE clusters, enabling application deployment without granting full cluster-management or project-wide editor permissions. The Kubernetes Engine Service Agent role is for the GKE service agent, not a human developer.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to the Kubernetes API server](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/api-server-authentication) · [Google Kubernetes Engine roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/container)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a monitoring application that runs on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. The application needs credentials from a service account to collect performance data. However, your organization has a policy that forbids creating new service account keys. You must give the application access while adhering to Google-recommended security practices. What should you do?

options.text: Use your personal user credentials to authenticate the application, ensuring your account has the necessary permissions.
Create a new project, generate a service account key in the new project, and grant the service account the required IAM roles in the application project.
Override the organization policy in the project, and create a long-lived service account key in the GKE cluster.
Configure Workload Identity Federation to allow the application to impersonate a service account.

questions.explanation:
Workload Identity Federation for GKE lets Kubernetes workloads use IAM-authorized, short-lived credentials instead of service account key files. It can be configured to let the workload impersonate an IAM service account that has the required permissions, satisfying the no-key policy and following the recommended GKE authentication model.

**Learn more:** [About Workload Identity Federation for GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/workload-identity) · [Authenticate to Google Cloud APIs from GKE workloads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity)

questions.domain: Ensuring successful operation of a cloud solution
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are managing a new Google Cloud project for a web application. The web application runs on a Compute Engine VM, and your team has a strict budget. You have already created a Cloud Billing budget and configured an alert rule to send an email when 90% of the budget is used. You must ensure that project spending automatically stops when it exceeds the budgeted amount. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new Cloud Billing account, and associate the project with it to prevent new spending from affecting your project’s budget.
Create a Pub/Sub topic, and connect it to the budget. Create a Cloud Run function that subscribes to the Pub/Sub topic and executes code to stop the VM.
Use the Cloud Billing dashboard to identify the forecasted spend of your project, and then update the budget and alert to match the forecasted spend.
Rely on the budget’s configuration to automatically disable billable resources when the spend reaches 100%.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Billing budgets alert on spend but do not automatically cap usage or disable billable resources. Programmatic budget notifications can be sent to a Pub/Sub topic, and a Cloud Run function triggered from that topic can stop Compute Engine VM instances after the budget is exceeded, eliminating the VM's ongoing compute charges.

**Learn more:** [Control resource usage with notifications](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/control-usage) · [Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/budgets)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The Human Resources department at your company publishes a BigQuery dataset containing anonymized information about company sales and products. All company employees are managed in the `terramearth.com` Cloud Identity account and must be able to view this dataset as authenticated users. You need to give every employee in the company read-only access to this BigQuery dataset. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the domain:terramearth.com principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.
Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the allUsers principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.
Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to a new service account on the dataset’s IAM policy.
Grant the roles/bigquery.dataViewer role to the allAuthenticatedUsers principal on the dataset’s IAM policy.

questions.explanation:
A domain principal for `terramearth.com` grants access to all identities in that Cloud Identity domain without exposing the dataset to users outside the company. At the dataset level, `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` grants read access to the dataset and its contained data resources.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery IAM roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control) · [Control access to resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/control-access-to-resources-iam)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An application reads data from a Pub/Sub topic. During local development, you used your personal credentials to authenticate and test the application. You now want to deploy it to Vertex AI and have created a new service account to serve as the application's identity. You need to ensure that the deployed application can continue accessing the Pub/Sub topic. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the relevant IAM roles to the service account used as your agent identity.
Generate a JSON private key for the service account, and upload the key as Vertex AI metadata.
Extract your access token by using the gcloud auth print-access-token command, and store it with the application.
Create a secret in Secret Manager to store your personal credentials, and configure the application’s authentication code to use this secret.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud services use the attached service account as the workload identity. Pub/Sub access is controlled through IAM roles granted to that service account; a workload that consumes messages needs the relevant Pub/Sub permissions, commonly the Pub/Sub Subscriber role on the applicable subscription. Production workloads should use service-account IAM authorization rather than embedded private keys, temporary user tokens, or personal credentials.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to Pub/Sub](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/authentication) · [Receive messages from a pull subscription](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/pull-messages)

questions.domain: Configuring access and security
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing an application on your personal workstation that will be hosted in Google Cloud. You are authenticated with a Google Account (USER). You need to test whether a particular set of permissions assigned to an existing service account (SERVICE_ACCOUNT) is sufficient for a task, without handling sensitive secret information. What should you do?

options.text: Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
Grant USER the IAM role roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on SERVICE_ACCOUNT.

questions.explanation:
Service account impersonation lets a user test actions using an existing service account’s IAM permissions while relying on short-lived credentials instead of service account keys. The Service Account Token Creator role (`roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`) grants the permissions required to create those credentials and to use `gcloud` service-account impersonation.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate to IAM](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/authentication) · [Roles for service account authentication](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-permissions)
